rationale.conceptual: The HMPP kernel is a custom method with several interacting components: localized graphs with Gaussian-weighted adjacency, a modified Floyd-Warshall algorithm for maximum probability paths, Coulomb label vectors, and a hybrid kernel combining two Laplacian sub-kernels. Correct implementation requires genuine understanding of the method and non-trivial math, not just applying off-the-shelf routines.
rationale.execution: The pipeline spans 4 stages (data preparation, hyperparameter grid search, training KRR on four subset sizes, evaluation), all within Python using standard libraries (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn). While not extremely fragile, the custom kernel implementation and multi-stage workflow make it a moderately complex execution.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a non-trivial custom graph kernel (HMPP) with multiple interacting components (Gaussian-weighted adjacency, modified Floyd-Warshall, Coulomb labels, hybrid Laplacian kernels) and performing a grid search for five hyperparameters, followed by KRR training and evaluation on multiple train sizes. The method is novel to the paper and demands careful translation of equations into code. The pipeline is moderate (~4 stages) with standard libraries but the custom kernel work elevates conceptual difficulty.

compute_estimate.reasoning: QM7 dataset is small (7165 molecules, up to 23 atoms); kernel matrices for up to 1000 training points are modest; CPU-only computation with few GB of RAM.
